Stories.title: The Lost Kingdom
Stories.author: Admin
Stories.description: A branching adventure where your decisions determine the fate of your journey.

nodes.title: The Village
nodes.text: You stand at the center of a mysterious village. Two paths lie before you.

nodes.title: The Dark Forest
nodes.text: The trees grow taller around you. You hear something moving in the shadows.

nodes.title: The Ancient Castle
nodes.text: You enter the castle and find the mysterious king waiting for you.

nodes.title: The Hidden Treasure
nodes.text: You follow the path and discover a legendary treasure hidden beneath the ancient trees.

nodes.title: Back to the Village
nodes.text: You safely return to the village. Perhaps another adventure awaits you.

nodes.title: The King's Victory
nodes.text: The king defeats you. Your journey ends inside the ancient castle.

Stories.title: THE HOLLOW MANOR MURDER
Stories.author: Admin
Stories.description:
Charles Ashford, wealthy owner of Hollow Manor, is found dead in his locked study during his annual dinner party. You are Detective Maya Reyes, called in that night. Five guests remain in the house.

Suspects:

Eleanor Ashford — the widow, set to inherit everything
Victor Cole — Charles's business partner, recently caught embezzling
Dr. Simon Wren — family physician, was having an affair with Eleanor
Priya Malhotra — Charles's estranged daughter, cut out of the will last month
Thomas Reed — the butler, been with the family 20 years

nodes.title: THE STUDY
nodes.text: The study is locked from inside. Charles lies by his desk, a letter opener in his chest. A whiskey glass sits half-full. The window is slightly open.

nodes.title: THE WOUND
nodes.text: The angle of the wound suggests the killer was left-handed and roughly Charles's height or shorter. No defensive wounds — he knew his attacker.

choices.text: Check who in the house is left-handed
Dust the letter opener for prints

nodes.title: THE WINDOW
nodes.text: Muddy footprints lead from the window to the rose bushes outside — but the mud is dry, at least a day old. A red herring; someone used this window earlier, unrelated to tonight.

choices.text: Dismiss the window and return to the body

nodes.title: QUESTIONING THOMAS REED
nodes.text: Thomas says he heard raised voices around 9 PM but couldn't make out words. He was polishing silver in the pantry — no alibi witness.

choices.text: Ask who else was near the study at 9 PM

nodes.title: LEFT-HANDED SUSPECTS
nodes.text: Victor Cole and Priya Malhotra are both left-handed. Eleanor and Dr. Wren are right-handed. Thomas is ambidextrous, an old detail from his military days.

nodes.title: FINGERPRINTS
nodes.text: The letter opener has been wiped clean — no prints at all. This tells you the killer was careful, not careless. Someone premeditated this, or panicked and thought fast.

choices.text: Ask the household who owns gloves

nodes.title: THOMAS UNDER PRESSURE
nodes.text: Thomas breaks slightly — admits the voices were Charles and Victor, arguing about "the missing forty thousand." He didn't mention it earlier out of loyalty.

choices.text: Ask Thomas if he's protecting someone else

nodes.title: WHO WAS NEARBY
nodes.text: Thomas recalls Dr. Wren walking toward the study around 8:50 PM, and Eleanor going upstairs shortly after. Priya was in the garden the whole evening, alone.

choices.text: Question Dr. Wren about the study visit

nodes.title: MISSED CLUE (Handedness Ignored)
nodes.text: Without the handedness detail, your suspect pool stays wide open and every later interrogation is weaker. You'll need extra evidence later to compensate.

choices.text: Move on to question the household

nodes.title: DEAD END
nodes.text:
You lose nearly an hour tracking a lead that goes nowhere. The real killer uses this time to destroy evidence.

Effect: One key clue is now burned and unavailable later.

choices.text: Give up on the footprints and return to the body

nodes.title: VICTOR COLE
nodes.text: Victor admits to the argument — Charles had discovered the embezzlement and threatened to go to the police that night. Victor swears he left the study alive at 9:05 PM and went straight to the bar for a drink. The bartender, a hired caterer, can't be found for confirmation yet.

choices.text: Track down the caterer to confirm the alibi
Arrest Victor now on motive and handedness alone
Keep him as a suspect, investigate Priya

nodes.title: PRIYA MALHOTRA
nodes.text: Priya, cut from the will, has clear motive but was seen by the gardener in the garden the entire night — except for a five-minute gap around 9 PM when she says she "walked to clear her head." No witness for those five minutes.

choices.text: Ask the gardener to pin down the exact gap timing

nodes.title: THOMAS'S SECRET
nodes.text: Digging into Thomas's file, you learn he was quietly written out of an earlier version of Charles's will years ago after a dispute — a grudge no one else knew about. He's left-leaning ambidextrous, technically fitting the wound profile.

choices.text: Confront Thomas directly with this history
Treat this as a minor detail and refocus on Victor/Priya

nodes.title: THE GLOVES
nodes.text: A pair of Eleanor's leather gloves is found in the study wastebasket — burned slightly at the fingertips, as if someone tried to destroy trace evidence. Eleanor claims she "hasn't worn those in months."

choices.text: Have them tested for GSR/trace fiber first

nodes.title: ELEANOR ASHFORD
nodes.text: Eleanor is composed, almost too composed. She admits the marriage was unhappy and she knew about Charles's affairs, but denies killing him. She says she went upstairs at 9 PM to "get some air" — no one saw her go up or come down.

choices.text: Push on the burned gloves (if found)
Arrest Eleanor now on opportunity and demeanor alone

nodes.title: THOMAS CONFESSES A DIFFERENT SECRET
nodes.text: Thomas isn't the killer — but he saw something. Around 9 PM, through the hallway window, he saw Dr. Wren leaving the study wiping his hands on a handkerchief. He stayed quiet out of fear of losing his position for gossiping about the family.

choices.text: Confront Dr. Wren with this eyewitness account

nodes.title: DR. SIMON WREN
nodes.text: Confronted, Wren cracks. He'd gone to ask Charles for money to "start over" with Eleanor once they left together — Charles laughed at him and threatened to expose the affair publicly, ruining his medical license. In the heat of it, Wren grabbed the letter opener. He wiped it clean out of pure panic, then dropped Eleanor's gloves (taken earlier that day after an affair rendezvous) into the wastebasket by mistake, burning the tips later in a candle to destroy fiber evidence.

choices.text: You have eyewitness (Thomas), motive, and physical evidence — arrest Dr. Wren
You feel the case is still circumstantial and hold off

nodes.title: THE CATERER
nodes.text: You track down the caterer. She confirms Victor was at the bar getting a drink from 9:03 PM onward — he could not have made it back upstairs in time. Victor is cleared of opportunity.

nodes.title: PRIYA'S ROOM
nodes.text: Nothing incriminating — just old family photos and a diary expressing hurt over being cut from the will, not rage. This softens her as a suspect but proves nothing either way.

choices.text: Head back to check her alibi

nodes.title: THE LEDGER (if not burned)
nodes.text: If NODE 10 was avoided, you find Charles's private ledger showing he'd also discovered irregular payments to Dr. Wren — hush money for staying quiet about something medical. This adds early suspicion toward Wren well before NODE 17.

choices.text: Bring the ledger into your questioning

nodes.title: THE GARDENER'S TIMELINE
nodes.text: The gardener confirms Priya's five-minute gap was spent by the fountain, visible from the kitchen window — the kitchen maid backs this up. Priya is cleared of opportunity entirely.

choices.text: Return to investigating Eleanor and Wren

nodes.title: FORENSICS RESULT
nodes.text: Trace fiber testing on the burned gloves finds skin cells matching Dr. Wren's — he wore Eleanor's gloves briefly, likely to avoid leaving prints, then panicked and disposed of them.

choices.text: Confront Dr. Wren with the evidence

nodes.title: HESITATION
nodes.text: Without an arrest, Dr. Wren has enough time overnight to destroy the handkerchief and flee the county by morning. The case goes cold.

nodes.title: ENDING A — CASE SOLVED (Correct Person)
nodes.text: Dr. Simon Wren is arrested and, faced with the eyewitness account, forensic gloves, and motive, confesses fully. Charles Ashford's murder is solved. Eleanor is devastated but relieved the truth is out.

nodes.title: ENDING B — WRONG PERSON (Victor Cole)
nodes.text: Victor is arrested on motive and handedness alone. Weeks later, the caterer surfaces and confirms his alibi. Victor is released, the real killer has fled, and your reputation takes a hit.

nodes.title: ENDING C — WRONG PERSON (Eleanor Ashford)
nodes.text: Eleanor is arrested on opportunity and demeanor. Her lawyer tears the case apart in court — no physical evidence ties her to the murder. She's acquitted, and the real killer, Dr. Wren, is never investigated again.

nodes.title: ENDING D — CASE UNSOLVED
nodes.text: Insufficient evidence and hesitation let the true killer escape before arrest. Charles Ashford's murder joins the county's cold case files.

traversalPath.title: QUESTIONING THOMAS REED
traversalPath.choiceText: Move on to question the household

traversalPath.title: ENDING B — WRONG PERSON (Victor Cole)
traversalPath.choiceText: Arrest Victor now on motive and handedness alone

traversalPath.title: LEFT-HANDED SUSPECTS
traversalPath.choiceText: Check who in the house is left-handed

The astral sanctuary ending gave me chills. The ambient soundscape matched the mysterious forest mood perfectly!
Peak cyberpunk atmosphere. The zero-day exploit branch leading to AI singularity was brilliant.
A masterclass in temporal causality and graph loops. The minimap visualization during reading is game-changing.
Classic gothic Agatha Christie vibe with modern interactive branching. Loved unmasking the heir!
